All three files are explicitly benign: (1) /notes.txt is 2024-05-06 department meeting notes (attendees wangfang, liqiang, zhoujie; topics Q2 budget review, office relocation, training plan) and states verbatim "No financial transactions were discussed"; (2) /docs/travel_reimbursement_form.txt is a blank sample template with underscores only, stating "This is a blank template. No personal data"; (3) /expense_policy.txt is a legitimate company policy v3 (30-day receipt submission, manager approval above 5000 CNY, Friday payment processing). The only timeline activity is three FILE_CREATED events within a 9-second window (1790556664–1790556673) forming a single cluster, consistent with files being written into the image, not with interactive user activity. No registry hives, Event Logs, Prefetch, Amcache, ShimCache, browser history, email, documents, logs, deleted files, or any execution traces are present. The Windows-specialist mission dimensions (account usage, execution traces, persistence, device activity, file activity) are therefore entirely unassessable from this acquisition. Two critical caveats: the task metadata reports platforms=[] and source_scopes=[], so no Windows scenario was actually registered and the delegated 'windows' scope is not backed by any registered source; and the file paths in the evidence previews point to a Linux build/data/extracted_files directory, indicating the image was processed as generic filesystem extraction rather than Windows artifact parsing. Consequently the correct conclusion is absence-of-evidence, not evidence-of-absence: the device cannot be cleared of financial fraud based on this acquisition alone.
